scope: Baseline-aware comparison, correction, reproof, output checking, status preservation, and human-owned proof release.

rules.title: Use the highest applicable proof authority
rules.assertion: Approved manuscript, chapter profile, production decisions, release policy, and current correction/variation records control proof classification.
forbidden_claims: generic proof preference overrides approved decision

rules.title: Generic preference cannot authorize a change
rules.assertion: A proofreading preference or model inference may generate a question but cannot authorize a correction or release change.

rules.title: Block missing proof preconditions
rules.assertion: Baseline, proof/output IDs, proof scope, approved variations, upstream statuses, authorized correction channel, format target, escalation path, and signatory must be recorded before substantive review.

rules.title: Capture baseline and fixity
rules.assertion: Approved manuscript/copyedited version, proof, output, assets, and correction cycles require stable IDs and hash/fixity or stable identifiers with capture events.
forbidden_claims: filename or timestamp alone proves identity

rules.title: Do not certify when baseline is unavailable
rules.assertion: An inaccessible baseline, asset, or required source remains source_unavailable or blocked; no defect-free or release claim may be made.

rules.title: Pause for corrupt or incomplete proof
rules.assertion: Missing pages, assets, fonts, sections, or corrupted output pauses detailed review and routes production.
forbidden_claims: partial proof is sufficient for final release

rules.title: Consult approved variations before defect classification
rules.assertion: Line breaks, placement, blank pages, styling, and other differences are not defects when supported by an approved design or production variation.

rules.title: Record exact current and expected state
rules.assertion: Each finding states exact visible current state, expected baseline/approved state, locator, evidence, authority, impact, and owner.

rules.title: Protect text and symbols in comparison
rules.assertion: Compare words, names, diacritics, scripts, numbers, signs, equations, code, glyphs, quotes, dashes, units, and special characters against the protected baseline.

rules.title: Escalate meaning-bearing substitutions
rules.assertion: A change affecting meaning, data, credit, attribution, source identity, or statistical notation is high or critical and requires human approval and reproof.

rules.title: Check navigation and layout objects
rules.assertion: TOC, headings, running elements, page numbers, breaks, footnotes, placeholders, index references, and reading flow are compared against the applicable design and baseline.
forbidden_claims: page flow is irrelevant to release

rules.title: Do not redesign at proof stage
rules.assertion: Aesthetic or intentional layout choices route to production; proof review does not redesign the book or change content to solve page flow without authority.

rules.title: Reconcile visual objects and companion records
rules.assertion: Figures, tables, captions, notes, legends, source lines, assets, placement, numbering, and format presence are linked to stable object records.

rules.title: Do not certify visual or rights quality from appearance
rules.assertion: Visual comparison may flag crop, reversal, missing content, or asset mismatch, but technical accuracy, permission, consent, and final quality remain delegated decisions.

rules.title: Check visible reference survival
rules.assertion: Visible citations, reference entries, notes, URLs, DOI displays, and fixed targets are compared with the accepted version and output.

rules.title: Preserve RCI and TE ownership
rules.assertion: RCI owns citation/source metadata integrity and TE owns semantic cross-reference structure; PPR routes substantive issues and checks visible survival only.
forbidden_claims: PPR certifies DOI or source status

rules.title: Require exact correction records
rules.assertion: Every correction includes unique ID, location, current state, replacement/action, reason, requester, owner, decision, incorporation output, reproof scope, and result.

rules.title: Preserve the correction state machine
rules.assertion: Corrections transition through open, clarified, accepted/rejected/deferred/referred, incorporated, reproof_required, reproof_passed, and resolved; any state can be blocked.

rules.title: Require incorporation and reproof for closure
rules.assertion: An accepted correction is resolved only after incorporation evidence and independent reproof of the affected scope pass.

rules.title: Retain rejected and deferred corrections
rules.assertion: Rejected, deferred, and referred corrections remain in the log with rationale and are not erased.

rules.title: Check each in-scope output format
rules.assertion: PDF, e-book, HTML, and other in-scope formats receive format-specific checks for navigation, reading order, headings, links, tables, alt text, language, and extraction as applicable.
forbidden_claims: one format pass covers all formats

rules.title: Do not claim accessibility conformance from visual check
rules.assertion: A visual proof check may report a signal or missing evidence, but formal conformance requires the designated specialist and applicable normative target.

rules.title: Link post-publication update to original
rules.assertion: A released error or update preserves original fixity and creates linked correction, version, status, notice, effective-date, and reader-communication records.

rules.title: Do not decide retraction or removal
rules.assertion: PPR records and communicates an authorized correction, withdrawal, removal, retraction, or expression-of-concern decision; it does not adjudicate that status.

rules.title: Carry unresolved material issues into release gate
rules.assertion: Open queries, failed reproofs, missing baseline, ambiguous file identity, high/critical findings, unapproved status changes, and unresolved upstream issues prevent release.

rules.title: Require human signatory and final fixity
rules.assertion: Release requires a final identity/fixity record, release event, named human signatory, decision ID, and retained evidence unless MWM explicitly delegates authority.

rules.title: Protect proofing channels and sensitive material
rules.assertion: Unpublished proofs, author correspondence, correction files, sensitive data, rights documents, and accidental external sharing are handled through authorized channels and incident routes.
forbidden_claims: public link is acceptable for internal proof

rules.title: Use the smallest authorized correction
rules.assertion: Correction instructions restore the approved text, meaning, object, or production requirement with the smallest change and no unapproved reflow or substantive rewrite.
forbidden_claims: proof stage is another writing pass

rules.title: Route unapproved author alterations
rules.assertion: A new section, substantive rewrite, or major author alteration beyond approved proof limits becomes a query, hold, or senior decision rather than a routine correction.

rules.title: Allow evidence-backed no action
rules.assertion: Harmless line breaks, approved blank pages, valid URL wraps, and approved low-resolution proof previews may close with no action when evidence supports them.

rules.title: Never silently overwrite the version of record
rules.assertion: Minor and significant updates preserve version lineage, supersession, fixity, and linked notices; the original record is retained.
